sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 1176.4 ± 314.2 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Auto-proteolytic (GAIN domain self-cleavage) activity confirmed intact by expression in COS-7 cells (L12); surface display confirmed by SpyCatcher engagement assay (L11); mutant variants (H381S, T383A, F385A, L388A/M389A) also expressed as surface receptors (L13), demonstrating the N-terminal tag does not impair trafficking or GPCR function.
sites.rationale: L14 explicitly states the SpyTag and HaloTag were introduced 'downstream of the signal peptide sequence' in the full-length ADGRG1 cDNA, which maps unambiguously to insert_after_residue=25 (the last residue of the signal peptide, G25, with the mature N-terminus R26 immediately following). Python confirms res(25)='G' and res(26)='R'. L12 validates intact auto-proteolytic activity and L11 confirms surface display, giving the highest validation tier. Full-length ADGRG1 (SpyTag-HaloTag-G1-EGFP) expressed in COS-7 cells; L14 states SpyTag and HaloTag were introduced 'downstream of the signal peptide sequence in the cDNA', placing both tags immediately after the SP cleavage site (residue 25/26 junction). L11 confirms surface display on migrating COS-7 cells engaging SpyCatcher-coated surfaces.

sources.claim: A SpyTag and HaloTag were introduced downstream of the signal peptide sequence in the cDNA to generate the SpyTag-HaloTag-G1-WT-EGFP construct.

The myc-tagged GPR56 wild-type (GPR56 WT) vector (pIRESpuro3-myc-hGPR56) encoding amino acids 26 to 693 was previously described ( 13 ) and the mutant GPR56ΔSTP vector (pIRESpuro3-myc-hGPR56ΔSTP) lacking the STP domain was generated in a similar manner.

literature_notes: Two extracellular surface tag sites were identified, both at the same junction (insert_after_residue=25, the mature N-terminus after SP cleavage). They are reported as separate entries because they derive from independent papers with different tags and different validation levels. L9 (C-terminal EGFP) was excluded from sites because the C-terminus of ADGRG1 is intracellular (topology landmarks: residues 658–693 are intracellular); it is recorded in other_positions. L15 (GAIN domain Q115–E395 in pDisplay) was excluded because it is a domain fragment construct, not a full-length membrane-anchored receptor, violating the 'full-length and membrane-anchored' requirement. L8 ('HaloTag N-terminal to the PLL domain') is consistent with L14 ('downstream of the signal peptide sequence') and does not indicate a separate internal insertion site; the PLL domain begins after the STP domain (~residue 178), but 'N-terminal to PLL' in the context of the NTF simply describes the overall NTF location, not a specific internal loop insertion. No ledger evidence supports an internal loop insertion in ECL1 (463–476), ECL2 (540–567), or ECL3 (629–636) for ADGRG1.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal EGFP fusion to full-length ADGRG1; the C-terminus (residues 658–693) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
